text: When a CLI tool wraps a git commit, extract identity args into a pure `build_commit_args()`-style helper so unit tests can assert the inline `-c user.name/user.email` flags without running git; the integration test then runs the full CLI against a stripped-identity env to close the gap.

When a prompt-assembly.js enrichment reads data from disk, the I/O helper belongs in orchestrator.js (fail-soft, try/catch per item) while the pure renderer in prompt-assembly.js stays fs-free and accepts the data as a caller-supplied map — see agentSkillDescriptions + skillsSection pattern in PR #618.

For AC6 (preview == seed) in CLAUDE.md composition features: both `saveAgentPrompt` and the `/internal/agents/:id/prompt-preview` endpoint must be updated to pass the same enrichment data to buildAgentClaudeMd — verify both call sites in every prompt-assembly PR.

When a dialog has single vs multi-item phrasing, use a derived boolean flag (e.g. `single = aggregated && count <= 1`) to branch copy only — leave controls, submit logic, and checkbox behaviour untouched; the flag is purely presentational.

When threading graph-node data from a section component into a dialog (e.g. teamSkills for extend-target picker), pass it as a second argument to the callback prop (onReviewSuggestion(s, skills)) and store it on the state object that opens the dialog — single source of truth, no separate fetch needed.

Two-sided module pattern (skill-manifest, knowledge-digest): when reviewing, run 'node --test' on BOTH test suites and verify byte-identical guard (test case that diffs the two files) passes — this is the only automated drift detector between admin-console and orchestrator copies.

skill-manifest.js copy semantics: stampSkillCopy (promote/lift/share) discards the cpSync-dragged skill.json before re-stamping (fresh v1 chain + origin); stampSkill (import, edit, create) reads any existing manifest and continues the chain — concept §3.1 / §3.5. Verify correct choice when reviewing any new copy-creating path.

When a new optional field is added to a two-sided JS+Python KB store, the KEY_ORDER, makeKnowledgeEntry/build_entry, and validateKnowledgeEntry must all be updated in BOTH mirrors and both cross-runtime GOLDEN tests must pass — no summary field emitted when absent means serialisation is byte-identical to pre-PR output.

Carry-forward pattern for re-projection-derived fields (summary, #635): read prior canonical files before re-projecting, carry each entry's field forward only when prev.text === e.text, so a text change drops the stale field and triggers regeneration on the next write pass.

When a PR adds a new UI action that supersedes an existing button, the old button must be removed in the same PR — leaving both co-existing fails the 'no-provenance paths gone from UI' criterion and creates a confusing dual-action UI (seen in PR #638 team→global: two buttons, one without provenance).

When reviewing a skill-tier engine PR (#626 pattern), always check KnowledgeFlow.jsx fetch() calls — the ShareDialog and lift path use /api/knowledge/share-to-team and /api/knowledge/promote which are separate from /api/skills/transfer; the issue key-files list is the reliable guide to which files must be changed.

core-sdlc.json label schema: humanGate=true means a human applies the label (e.g. 'ready'); humanGate=false means an agent applies it; brake=true means the label pauses the automated loop pending a human decision (e.g. 'human-decision-required'); brake=false means it is a routing signal only.

When an issue lists KnowledgeFlow.jsx as a key file alongside a permission-gating AC for Team Admins, verify BOTH the backend gate AND the frontend route guard — AdminRoute (user.admin = sysadmin/envAdmin only) blocks Team Admins from SkillsRegistry; the fix belongs in either the route or KnowledgeFlow.jsx.

Deep-link via query param pattern (e.g. ?session=<correlationId>): consume in AgentChat.jsx once agents load with a consumedRef guard; propagate via a *Request state (with ts: Date.now() for re-trigger); the receiving panel does its own fresh API fetch with a cancel flag so stale async results never update state after unmount.

Skill deletion archive (skill-deletion.js #627): DELETE takes a snapshot BEFORE the guard check; snapshot is rolled back on 409 so a refused cascade never leaves an orphan archive — the ordering is intentional and must be preserved in future delete-path changes.

skill-import.js anti-drift guard: skill-import.test.js asserts parseFrontmatterField(c, 'description') === parseSkillDescription(c) across 6 canonical cases — run this test when touching either parser to catch cross-module drift (issue #628, PR #646).

forceHistory:true on stampSkill/stampSkillDir appends a history entry and refreshes updatedAt/updatedBy without bumping version — the correct stamp for a provenance-only lifecycle event (import round-trip) where content is byte-identical; additive and default-off, mirrored into both byte-identical skill-manifest.js copies (PR #646).

When a skill-drift feature overlays drift state on the API list and knowledge graph, all three edit paths (PUT /api/skills/:name team branch, global branch, and PUT /api/skills/:name/file) must call autoResyncOnEdit — missing one leaves a silent gap in the auto-resync fan-out.

Drift is a property of copies (seeded agent workspace replicas, team copies of a global skill), not sources — drift badges belong on the Knowledge graph surface (KnowledgeFlow.jsx SkillCard) where member copies are visible, not on the Skills Registry where source pool skills are managed.

When an install/copy endpoint is replaced by a delegation to the orchestrator's activate path, remove the admin-console containment check for the source dir (now handled by the orchestrator's resolveSkillSourceDir) but keep the containment check for the destination dir — CodeQL tracks the inflow in api.js, not the delegated path.

planAgentGrantEdit (#630): team-member must materialise the full effective (inherited) grant into skillsOverride before appending — failing to do so silently drops all inherited team skills from the member's grant. The test case 'materializing the inherited grant' is the key regression guard.

For operator-triggered destructive git actions in the admin-console proxy, the AC7 running-session re-check belongs at the proxy layer (reads running-sessions.json directly before forwarding) — not duplicated in the orchestrator endpoint, since the proxy is the single control-plane gate before git commands run (#648 pattern).

When a Workspace Git panel endpoint enriches GET /api/agents/:id/workspace/git-status with branch metadata (currentBranch, branches[], detached, hasRemote, hasUpstream, dirty), derive those fields from a pure read-only helper (readRepoBranchMeta) that runs only local git commands and spreads into the existing response shape — keeps the status endpoint non-breaking and avoids a separate endpoint (#648).

Skill merge (#631) pure-planner pattern: skill-merge.js is fs-free (pure validator + planner), api.js does all IO — same 'pure core + IO caller' discipline as skill-transfer.js / skill-deletion.js; the stampSkillCopy (fresh v1 chain) is correct for a merge because the merged skill is a new entity.

In POST /api/skills/merge grant migration, the target skill must be activated FIRST via the orchestrator (before deactivating each source) so no member workspace is left without the skill during the transition window.

Token telemetry run_context must be built on ALL call paths (cron, github-event, http, DM) — the DM path in phase 1 omits it, leaving trigger/github null on DM records; flag as a follow-up when reviewing phase 2 token attribution.

For new telemetry endpoints, verify the golden fixture covers the null/None case for every optional field (trigger, github, modelUsage) — the aggregator's handling of null values should be tested explicitly alongside the structured-value cases.

When reviewing a PR branch that accumulated multiple preceding merged sub-PRs, diff against the last merged PR's merge-base commit (git diff <last-merge-sha>...HEAD) rather than origin/main to isolate only the new work — the three-dot diff is the right tool.

Lazy lineage fetch pattern in SkillViewer (#632): reset lineage to null on skill change (skillKey effect), fetch only when tab !== 'content' and lineage is null — a single round-trip gate so file browsing stays fast.

For work-item attribution PRs: verify the pr-events graph-building pass reads ALL pr-events records WITHOUT a `since` window filter — a PR opened before the query window still owns runs inside it; only the usage-run pass is windowed by since/until.

Tier-C (branch) attribution proxy for agent authorship: require `rec.git.headAfter !== rec.git.headBefore` (HEAD moved = agent committed); no @agents.local author-field check needed because only agent runs emit usage records.

When a phased-feature branch (phase N) is built on top of an unmerged phase-(N-1) branch, git diff origin/main...HEAD spans both phases; use git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD to enumerate each commit and git show <sha> --stat to isolate the new work from the prerequisite foundation before writing the AC verdict.

When reviewing a grant-validation PR, check POST /api/agents/:teamId/members as a gap — it accepts skillsOverride but bypasses any /api/agents/:id validation. It is typically out of issue scope (not in key files) but worth a non-blocking note.

SkillPicker v2 prop interface (PR #662): `skills` (array of skill objects, not names), `selected` (array of names), `onChange`, optional `emptyHint`. buildRows collapses to one row per name (team-first) and appends unknown selected names as flagged rows.

When reviewing a shared-core extraction PR (e.g. commitSkillWrite #639), enumerate all callers and verify each passes the correct stamp.mode — 'chain' for in-place extend (continues existing chain), 'copy' for all new-instance paths (fresh v1 chain, discards dragged manifest). A wrong mode silently breaks skill lineage.
For CI-only PRs, the meaningful diff is just the new workflow file — use 'git show <top-commit-sha>' to isolate scope, as the branch may include many already-merged commits if it was cut behind main.

When a new Node package (e.g. e2e/) installs via `npm ci` in the Makefile/CI, verify `package-lock.json` is committed — its absence is the most common silent break for a new harness (seen in PR #675).

For E2E-phase PRs whose runtime-dependent ACs cannot be verified from the sandbox (no podman/browser), the reviewer still blocks on the concrete code-level prerequisite (missing lockfile) and requires a `workflow_dispatch` green run before approving.

When a wizard step and a settings page share the same auth UI (e.g. OAuthLoginWizard), extract it to src/components/ as a shared component imported by both — this is the implementation pattern for an AC8-style 'two surfaces must not drift' requirement.

For wizard steps that use shared payload logic (build + gate), extract both helpers to a sibling .js file (e.g. setup-wizard-payload.js) free of React/DOM so they can be tested with node --test — the wizard save-gate and the payload builder must be driven by the same function to prevent drift.
